svg.title: Part 11 in one minute 4 · bit flips
svg.desc: 2,367 single bit flips in PicoRV32; 19.3 % changed a result, the rest were masked.
svg.text: most flips land in a value that is overwritten
x3 bit 22 flips, then x3 is written again before anyone reads it
x6 bit 11 flips and the next instruction reads x6
flips that changed a result, per sub-part
A software test can't wait for a random flip.
Transient faults need hardware that checks every access:
parity or ECC on registers and memory, or a lockstep second core.
Most flips vanish. The rest need hardware, not software.
PicoRV32 (ISC) synthesised with Yosys to sky130_fd_sc_hd (Apache-2.0); one flip per flip-flop at a random cycle of our self-test.
'Changed a result' = visible on the memory bus during the test. Counters score high because the test reads them.

g.text: Terms: ALU arithmetic logic unit: the part of a processor that adds, compares and shifts · CPU central processing unit:
a processor core · ECC error-correcting code (memory) · IRQ interrupt request · ISC ISC licence: a short permissive
